subject: Next steps: PoC mode decision & trial checklist for EdgeHealth
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: carla.mendez@edgehealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Next steps: PoC mode decision & trial checklist for EdgeHealth

Hi Carla / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions for the PoC and the deployment-mode choice (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Recap from our discussion:
- EdgeHealth use case: realtime clinical summarization + semantic search across patient notes (latency sensitive, must meet ~300ms 95th percentile per request at pilot scale).
- Data sensitivity: PHI in scope but scoped to de-identified/stored logs for the pilot; long-term preference is Private VPC if regulatory gates require it.
- Likely throughput for pilot: ~15 qps peak, 1.2M tokens/day estimate.

Key asks we need answered to pick the deployment mode and scope the PoC:
1) Primary blocker: security approval timeline from your InfoSec team — are they open to a short security self-host checklist for a Private trial, or would you prefer we run a Dedicated reserved environment first?
2) Success criteria (please confirm): 300ms 95th latency, >99% uptime during business hours, end-to-end correctness on 200 validation prompts with >95% pass rate. We captured these in the attached 'poc-success-metrics.xlsx' — please add/edit.
3) Pilot timeline: target 6 weeks end-to-end starting technical kickoff. Do you have firm blackout windows or procurement cycles we should align to?
4) Internal stakeholders: you mentioned Samir (CTO) + Security lead + Clinical ML owner. Please confirm names and their availability for a kickoff.

Proposed PoC plan (high level):
- Week 0: legal & procurement (SLA and basic terms) + security questionnaire
- Week 1: infra prep (choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC; if Private, start network onboarding)
- Weeks 2–3: integration + baseline performance tests (latency + throughput)
- Weeks 4–5: validation on your production-like prompts + QA evaluation
- Week 6: wrap-up, findings, and recommended path to production (with estimated TCO for each mode)

Attachments: poc-success-metrics.xlsx (success criteria sheet), redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf (network steps if you pick Private). I've also attached a preliminary cost delta CSV for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Can you confirm: preferred deployment mode to explore first for the PoC (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), the names of the 3 internal stakeholders we should loop in, and whether a 6-week pilot window works?

I propose a quick 30-min kickoff on Wed 26 May 10:00am PT if that works for your team.

Thanks —

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer\\Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---

From: Carla Mendez <carla.mendez@edgehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgehealth.com>, security@edgehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: PoC mode decision & trial checklist for EdgeHealth

Jonas —

Appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifying points from our side before we confirm the kickoff: 

1) Security: our Security team prefers Private VPC for anything touching PHI. That said, for the pilot they may accept a Dedicated environment if we get a network isolation and an executed data processing addendum quickly. I'm looping Samir and security@edgehealth.com to confirm.

2) Throughput: 15 qps peak is correct for pilot, but the long-term target is closer to 50 qps. Please include reference load ramps in your test plan.

3) Success criteria: the 300ms 95th pctl is aggressive — can you show an example benchmark (same model family) from your Hosted environment so we can evaluate the realistic expectation?

4) Stakeholders: Samir Patel (CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Data — priya.rao@edgehealth.com), and Maya Shah (InfoSec lead — maya.shah@edgehealth.com).

Procurement: we have a quarterly procurement window that closes 10 Jun; if we want a PO in June we need to move fast. 

We prefer to start with a Dedicated pool for the pilot (predictable throughput/timing) but will escalate to Private VPC if InfoSec requires it. Can you outline the minimal Dedicated configuration you recommend for 15 qps and estimated monthly commit?

Also — can you send a short one-pager describing the Private VPC onboarding steps (network peering, firewall rules, cert exchange)?

Thanks,

Carla
Head of Product Operations\EdgeHealth
carla.mendez@edgehealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0128

---

On Wed, 26 May 2027 16:30:00 +0000 Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
To: carla.mendez@edgehealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Next steps: PoC mode decision & trial checklist for EdgeHealth

Hi Carla — thanks, that all makes sense. Quick answers and a proposed minimal Dedicated spec + immediate deliverables.

Minimal Dedicated spec for 15 qps pilot (rough, we will bench to refine):
- 4x A100-equivalent GPUs in a small reserved pool (continuous) with autoscale headroom for brief spikes (estimate sustained 15 qps at target latency).
- KV cache enabled, sequence length cap 1024 for the pilot.
- Estimated commit: $20k–$28k/month depending on region and instance type (we'll provide a precise quote once you confirm region). See attached 'dedicated-vs-hosted-cost-estimate.csv'.

Hosted benchmark: we ran a 2k-prompt sample on a similar model and saw ~260ms 95th pctl on our Hosted API with caching enabled (attached summary). We can reproduce this on identical sample prompts during onboarding.

Immediate deliverables if you confirm Dedicated-first approach:
1) Security packet & quick answers for InfoSec (we'll close most items in 3 business days).
2) Dedicated configuration and formal quote (2 business days).
3) Technical kickoff and smoke test plan (schedule during Week 1).

If InfoSec requires Private VPC, the network checklist attached shows the minimal items: BGP or static routes, a temporary CIDR for the trial, and an SCP for egress policy. Private onboarding typically adds 2–3 weeks to the start of the PoC due to networking and access approvals.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm Dedicated-first and we open the procurement quote thread (target PO before 10 Jun).
- We schedule a 30-min kickoff Wed 26 May 10:00am PT (if that slot still works) to align on test prompts and access.

I will also loop in our Product Security contact if Maya wants a call.

Best,

Jonas

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: PoC mode decision & trial checklist for EdgeHealth

Carla / Samir —

Adding a couple concrete items from an ops perspective to make the Dedicated path low-friction: 

- Bench plan: 1) synthetic latency run (95/99) with your top 50 prompts, 2) load ramp to 50 qps for 10 minutes to validate autoscale headroom, 3) correctness sweep on the 200 validation prompts. We will provide the bench harness and a short script to run locally.
- Data handling: for the pilot we recommend tokens-in transit only; persistent logs stored encrypted and retained 30 days by default (we can adjust).
- Runbook & owners: Jonas -> integration + bench coordination; Aditya -> infra config + dedicated sizing; Lauren -> commercial + procurement follow-through.

Timeline constraints to hit PO by 10 Jun: we need confirmation by Thu 29 May EOD to have quote and PO paperwork completed on your side. If we get confirmation, we will prepare an invoice/quote and the security packet immediately.

Attachments delivered to this thread: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf, poc-success-metrics.xlsx, dedicated-vs-hosted-cost-estimate.csv.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the bench plan — Jonas, can you confirm Wed 26 May 10:00am PT or propose the next best slot?

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
